card.summary: Expona video portfolio on rob.expona.ai, served from the existing object store
card.description: The next-expona platform renders cinematic marketing films through mini-crew-service and stores them in Linode Object Storage: bucket expona-images (us-lax-1), keys videos/<job_id>/<file>.mp4 (cinematic.mp4, cinematic-graded.mp4, ...), public-read, with Range support. About 30 films exist today. Add a portfolio of these videos to rob.expona.ai: the Go backend lists and describes them, and the web app gets a /videos page where visitors watch and download them. No upload and no new storage; the bucket is the source of truth and is only read.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: GET /api/videos on the Go backend returns the portfolio as JSON, newest first: for each video an id (the job_id path segment), title, description, url (the public object URL), sizeBytes and lastModified. It is built by listing VIDEO_S3_BUCKET under VIDEO_S3_PREFIX (default videos/) with S3 ListObjectsV2 against VIDEO_S3_ENDPOINT, following continuation tokens.

AC2: Only real videos are listed: keys ending in .mp4, .webm or .mov whose stored Content-Type (from a HEAD request) is video/*. Objects that fail this check are skipped and logged once; for example videos/6129bfa4-.../product-demo.mp4 is really a PNG. When a job folder holds several videos, prefer cinematic-graded.mp4, then cinematic.mp4, then the newest file.

AC3: Titles and descriptions come from the curated catalog already committed at server/internal/video/catalog.json (27 entries, keyed by id: {title, description, hidden}), embedded into the binary with go:embed. hidden: true removes a video from the list. A video with no catalog entry is still listed, with the title 'Expona film' and its date (for example 'Expona film · 22 Aug 2026').

AC4: GET /api/videos/{id}/download responds 302 to a presigned GET URL for that object, valid for 15 minutes, with response-content-disposition=attachment and a filename of expona-<id>.mp4. An id not in the current listing returns 404; an id that is not a UUID returns 400. The id is never used to build an object key except by lookup in the listing.

AC5: The listing is cached in memory for VIDEO_CACHE_TTL (default 5 minutes), so a page view does not list the bucket. If the store is unreachable or VIDEO_S3_BUCKET is unset, /api/videos returns 503 with a JSON error, and the rest of the server (chat, /health) is unaffected.

AC6: GoReactChat web has a /videos page titled 'Expona portfolio', linked from the site navigation: a responsive grid of cards, each with an HTML5 player (preload=metadata, playsInline, controls) pointed at the public url, the title, the description, the date and a Download button that links to /api/videos/{id}/download. It has a loading state, an empty state and an error state.

AC7: Tests. Go: listing with pagination, the type filter and folder preference, catalog titles and the hidden flag, the default title, the cache, 503 on a store failure, and the download redirect (404 for an unknown id, 400 for a non-UUID, and the attachment disposition). Use an httptest S3 stub, never the real bucket. Web: rendering the grid from a fixture, the empty and error states, and the Download link.
guidance: Plain net/http handlers on the existing mux in server/cmd/lumid/main.go, not a ConnectRPC service. Put the logic in a new package server/internal/video and keep main.go to wiring. Use github.com/minio/minio-go/v7 for list, stat and presign; it works with Linode Object Storage, and next-expona uses the same client.

Never proxy video bytes through the API pod. Playback uses the public object URL directly, and download uses a presigned redirect. The pod is a single replica with strategy Recreate and must stay that way.

Configuration is environment only: VIDEO_S3_ENDPOINT (https://us-lax-1.linodeobjects.com), VIDEO_S3_REGION (us-lax-1), VIDEO_S3_BUCKET (expona-images), VIDEO_S3_PREFIX (videos/), VIDEO_S3_ACCESS_KEY and VIDEO_S3_SECRET_KEY, and VIDEO_CACHE_TTL. The keys are the existing Linode key labelled expona-images, injected from next-expona-app-secrets. It is not read-only, so use it only to list, stat and presign GETs; never write, delete or presign anything else. Never log them.

The browser calls the API same-origin with a relative /api/videos URL, as web/src/lib/chat-client.ts does. Video elements load from expona-images.us-lax-1.linodeobjects.com; if the app sets a Content-Security-Policy, add that origin to media-src only.

Reuse the existing Tailwind styling, including the dark: variants. Do not change the chat page, /catalog or /pipeline beyond adding the nav link. Videos are 16:9 and portrait-safe; use object-contain.
deploy/** is out of scope for agents. The ConfigMap values, the key injection and the /api/videos ingress route are already in deploy/ on main.
catalog.json is curated by the owner from the next-expona assets table. Read it, embed it, and test against your own fixture catalog; do not edit, reorder or regenerate it.

plan.summary: Add a read-only video portfolio. A new Go package, server/internal/video, lists the expona-images bucket with minio-go, filters and caches the result, and serves GET /api/videos and GET /api/videos/{id}/download as plain net/http handlers on the existing mux. The web app gets a /videos page ("Expona portfolio") with a responsive player grid, Download links and a link in the chat sidebar. No video bytes pass through the API pod, and nothing in deploy/ or catalog.json changes.
approach: api/config: add VideoS3Endpoint, VideoS3Region, VideoS3Bucket, VideoS3Prefix (default videos/, normalized to a trailing slash), VideoS3AccessKey, VideoS3SecretKey and VideoCacheTTL (default 5m, new envDuration helper; invalid or non-positive values fall back to the default, like envInt). None is required in validate(). Endpoint and region default to the sponsor's values; the bucket has no default.

api/store.go: define a narrow internal interface with list, stat and presignGet only, implemented over minio-go v7. No write, delete or other presign method is exposed. Set Region explicitly so there is no GetBucketLocation call, derive Secure from the endpoint scheme, use BucketLookupAuto (path style for Linode and for the httptest IP), and set MaxRetries to 1 so an outage fails fast. List with ListObjects Recursive, which is ListObjectsV2 and follows continuation tokens; cancel its context on early return. Never log keys or presigned URLs.

api/listing: accept only <prefix><uuid>/<file>, with the file ending in .mp4, .webm or .mov (case-insensitive). HEAD candidates with concurrency of at most 8 and keep those with Content-Type video/*. Non-video objects, and those whose HEAD returns 403 or 404, are skipped and logged once per key for the process lifetime. Any other HEAD or list error fails the refresh. Then, per folder, choose cinematic-graded.mp4, then cinematic.mp4, then the newest file. Sort by lastModified descending, tie-broken by id. The public url is <scheme>://<bucket>.<endpoint host>/<escaped key>.

api/catalog.go: go:embed catalog.json unchanged and parse it into a map; the service takes the catalog as a parameter so tests inject their own fixture. hidden removes the entry from the listing, so its download is 404. With no entry (or a blank title) the title is 'Expona film · 2 Jan 2006' from lastModified in UTC, and the description is empty.

api/service.go: mutex-guarded in-memory cache with injectable clock. Concurrent misses share one refresh, which runs on its own 15s-bounded context so a visitor disconnecting cannot fail it for others. After expiry, a failed refresh returns an error rather than stale data (AC5). Failures are remembered for 10s so an outage does not trigger a list per request.

api/handler.go: GET /api/videos returns {"videos":[{id,title,description,url,sizeBytes,lastModified}]} with RFC 3339 UTC dates and [] when empty. Failures return 503 {"error":"..."} with a generic message; details go to the log. Download checks a strict 36-character UUID first (400), then looks up the cached listing (404 unknown, 503 store failure), then returns 302 to a 15-minute presigned GET of the key from the listing, with response-content-disposition=attachment; filename="expona-<id>.mp4" and Cache-Control: no-store.

api/main.go: wiring only. Build the service from cfg and register both routes on the mux. An unset bucket, missing keys or an invalid endpoint logs a warning and registers handlers that return 503; boot never fails and never contacts the store.

web/lib: src/lib/videos.ts holds types, loadVideos(signal) returning a ready | empty | error state, downloadUrl(id) and a fixed-UTC formatDate. The base is NEXT_PUBLIC_LUMI_URL ?? "", matching chat-client.ts, so production uses relative URLs and local next dev works.

web/page: src/app/videos/page.tsx is a server shell with metadata and the 'Expona portfolio' heading; src/components/videos/video-portfolio.tsx is the client loader; src/components/videos/video-grid.tsx is presentational and takes the state (loading, empty, error, ready). Reuse the catalog page's Tailwind and dark: classes, with aspect-video object-contain players using controls, playsInline and preload=metadata, and a plain <a> styled as a Download button (not next/link, to avoid prefetching the API). Read the Next 16 docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs first, as web/AGENTS.md requires.

Nav: there is no shared site navigation, so the /videos link goes in the Sidebar of src/components/chat.tsx, which is the only existing navigation; /catalog and /pipeline stay untouched. No CSP is set in next.config.ts or the app, so no CSP change is needed.
Web tests use react-dom/server renderToStaticMarkup in the existing node Vitest environment, so no npm dependency or lockfile change is needed; vitest.config.mts include gains src/**/*.test.tsx.
Verification: in server, go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... (the 'lumid (Go backend)' check); in web, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test and npm run build (the web-ci check).

tests.name: server/internal/video/service_test.go: follows continuation tokens over multiple ListObjectsV2 pages under the prefix; newest first; correct fields and public URL (go test ./internal/video/...)

server/internal/video/service_test.go: extension and HEAD Content-Type filter, PNG named .mp4 skipped and logged once across refreshes, HEAD 404 skipped, non-UUID and nested keys ignored, folder preference applied after the filter (including a bad cinematic-graded.mp4 falling back)
server/internal/video/catalog_test.go: fixture titles and descriptions, hidden removed, dated default title; embedded catalog parses to 27 entries with UUID keys

server/internal/video/handler_test.go: 302 with X-Amz-Expires=900 and attachment filename expona-<id>.mp4 for the listed key; 404 for unknown and hidden ids; 400 for non-UUID and encoded traversal ids; stub sees only GET list and HEAD, no object GET
server/internal/video/service_test.go: one listing within TTL, re-list after expiry (fake clock), concurrent misses share one refresh, failure after expiry is an error

server/internal/video/handler_test.go: 503 JSON when the store fails, is unreachable, bucket is unset or keys are missing, and neither body nor logs contain the keys; a /health and a chat-like route on the same mux still return 200; list JSON shape and empty array
server/internal/config/config_test.go: VIDEO_* defaults, overrides, invalid TTL fallback, and Load succeeds with no VIDEO_* set
server build: go build ./... && go vet ./... with catalog.json embedded (lumid CI check)
web/src/lib/videos.test.ts: relative /api/videos URL, ready/empty/error mapping for 200, empty, 503 and network failure, download URL, UTC date (npm test)
web/src/components/videos/video-grid.test.tsx: fixture cards with player attributes and public src, title, description, date, Download href; loading, empty and error states (npm test)
web/src/app/videos/page.test.tsx and web/src/components/chat.test.tsx: 'Expona portfolio' heading with initial loading state; sidebar links to /videos (npm test)
web CI: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build

outOfScope: deploy/**, .github/**, .agentic/**, proto and migrations; pod replica and strategy settings
Uploads, new storage, thumbnails, transcoding, or proxying video bytes
Changes to the chat page, /catalog or /pipeline other than the single sidebar link
Per-request rate limiting or auth on /api/videos (public, like the page)
risks: The committed .agentic/pipeline.yaml enables agent development only for web, with server/** forbidden and only npm inner-loop commands. The api component may need an owner-side configuration change if that file governs this run.
Adding minio-go needs Go module network access in the coding sandbox, and go mod tidy may raise shared indirect versions such as golang.org/x/net; review the go.mod diff.
The Linode key has write access. The narrow store interface and the stub's method check limit the code to list, HEAD and presigned GET, but the credential itself is not restricted.
A cold or expired cache costs one list plus about 30 or more HEADs, so the first view every 5 minutes is slower (bounded by 15s).
Transient HEAD failures fail the whole refresh with 503, deliberately, instead of silently dropping films.

minio-go selects path-style URLs for presigning against Linode while playback uses the virtual-host URL; the real bucket is never touched in tests, so check one download and one playback after deployment.
Server-rendered markup tests do not exercise the browser effect that calls loadVideos; that wiring is kept minimal and the loader is tested separately.
Web and API live in one repo but may merge separately; until the API is deployed, /videos shows its error state.

web/page: src/app/videos/page.tsx is a server shell with metadata and the 'Expona portfolio' heading; src/components/videos/video-portfolio.tsx is the client loader; src/components/videos/video-grid.tsx is presentational and takes the state (loading, empty, error, ready). Reuse the catalog page's Tailwind and dark: classes, with aspect-video object-contain players using controls, playsInline and preload=metadata, and a plain <a> styled as a Download button (not next/link, to avoid prefetching the API). Read the Next 16 docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs first, as web/AGENTS.md requires.

Nav: there is no shared site navigation, so the /videos link goes in the Sidebar of src/components/chat.tsx, which is the only existing navigation; /catalog and /pipeline stay untouched. No CSP is set in next.config.ts or the app, so no CSP change is needed.
Web tests use react-dom/server renderToStaticMarkup in the existing node Vitest environment, so no npm dependency or lockfile change is needed; vitest.config.mts include gains src/**/*.test.tsx.
Verification: in server, go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... (the 'lumid (Go backend)' check); in web, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test and npm run build (the web-ci check).

risks: The committed .agentic/pipeline.yaml enables agent development only for web, with server/** forbidden and only npm inner-loop commands. The api component may need an owner-side configuration change if that file governs this run.
Adding minio-go needs Go module network access in the coding sandbox, and go mod tidy may raise shared indirect versions such as golang.org/x/net; review the go.mod diff.
The Linode key has write access. The narrow store interface and the stub's method check limit the code to list, HEAD and presigned GET, but the credential itself is not restricted.
A cold or expired cache costs one list plus about 30 or more HEADs, so the first view every 5 minutes is slower (bounded by 15s).
Transient HEAD failures fail the whole refresh with 503, deliberately, instead of silently dropping films.

minio-go selects path-style URLs for presigning against Linode while playback uses the virtual-host URL; the real bucket is never touched in tests, so check one download and one playback after deployment.
Server-rendered markup tests do not exercise the browser effect that calls loadVideos; that wiring is kept minimal and the loader is tested separately.
Web and API live in one repo but may merge separately; until the API is deployed, /videos shows its error state.
